title: Doing Righteousness, Doing Sin, and the Seed of God
english: …Whoever looks down on all these things will be above the world, doing the will of God by abiding forever and loving God (1 John 2:17).
He says this because, after becoming disciples, they departed from the truth (1 John 2:19) and invented blasphemies of their own devising.

Whoever has understood with true knowledge that God is righteous in his very being will at once know that the one who does his righteousness is born of him (1 John 2:29); just as the one who knows that he is holiness gives himself over to being made holy, since he understands exactly the saying, "You shall be holy, for I am holy" (1 Peter 1:16). It is well said, too, that he "does" righteousness, not that he "did" or "will do" it. Virtue, being a thing of practice, makes the one who exercises it righteous; so no one is righteous before he does it, nor is the one who has stopped acting by it. That God is righteous, Moses says: "Holy and righteous is the Lord" (Deuteronomy 32:4). He is the Father of the Savior: "Righteous Father, the world has not known you" (John 17:25). Being his Son, as God from God and holy from holy, he is likewise righteous from righteous. It is no contradiction that he is also said to be righteousness; for what is such in its very being may be called both righteousness and righteous.
"Now we are children of God" (1 John 3:2): that is, in the present life.

From Chrysostom: Since the devil turned away before anyone else and came to be in sin, everyone who acts sinfully is named as being of him. For he takes the lead in the one who sins by suggesting evil thoughts, as in the case of Judas.

But someone will say that the devil comes to be in sinners who had already sinned before him, by their giving him place. To this we must answer that doing sin is the same thing as sinning by giving place to the devil. For a man gives him place when, led on by desire, after receiving him, he carries out the sin in action; that is what "doing" it means. It is well said, too, that he "does" and not that he "did": the one who has repented is no longer of the devil, but only the one who is still committing it. So too it is the one who does sin, not the one who did it, who is the slave of sin: "For everyone who does sin," he says, "is its slave" (John 8:34).

From Severus: He also adds the reason why such a man cannot sin, saying that "his seed remains in him." What is the seed of God that remains upon the faithful? Is it not the coming of the Holy Spirit, through which we were born again? It does not leave us, so long as, in Paul's words, we do not grieve by shameful deeds the Holy Spirit of God, in whom we were sealed for the day of revelation.

For when we say that one who has righteousness cannot do wrong, we do not mean a natural inability, the kind by which we say that an irrational animal cannot have knowledge or anything else of that sort.

If everyone who does sin is of the devil (1 John 3:8), then by acting so he is shown to be a child of the devil, just as Elymas the magician was known to be a son of the devil from his being "full of all deceit" (Acts 13:10). And since everyone who has been born of God does not do sin, because he has the seed of God in himself (1 John 3:9), the one who does not sin in this way can clearly be found to be a son of God. I added "in this way" to "not sinning" so that no one may quibble and say that we count all who do not sin as children of God. Infants, for example, who do not do sin, are not to be called children of God: it is their age, not virtue, that keeps them from sinning. And that is without adding a further point, that it is not even sound to say of infants that they do not do sin. For not sinning is not the same as not doing sin: the one seems to be a bare negation, while the other comes from a settled disposition.

Since the one who does righteousness has been born of God, and loving the brothers follows for one so born, the one who does not have righteousness, because he does not do it, and who hates his brother, is not of God (1 John 3:10), in no other sense than that he has not been born of him. For no heed should be paid to those who say that such people are not of God because of an earthly nature.
For by "the world" here he means wicked people (1 John 3:13).

For in the same way as before the coming of Christ, when there were prophets of God in Judea, many happened to be feigning prophecy, so that a searching skill was needed to tell which of those who said "Thus says the Lord" had the Holy Spirit and the word of God, and which were prophets of falsehood, moved by an evil spirit (1 John 4:1); so also after the arrival of the apostles, who spoke in Christ and …

translator_notes: Copy-text: PG 39, In epistulas catholicas brevis enarratio, Greek fragments (Khazarzar transcription). Translated again clause by clause from the Greek on 11 Nov 2026: the earlier English left out the notes on 1 John 2:17-3:8 and dropped a negation in the note on 3:9.

The catena's fragment numbers and its locators ("Cr …", "Ma …") printed in the Greek are not translated. Its headings "Τοῦ Χρυσοστόμου" and "Σευήρου" are given as "From Chrysostom:" and "From Severus:"; those two notes stand under other writers' names in the catena.
"Who had already sinned before him" renders τῶν πρὸ αὐτοῦ ἡμαρτηκότων: the objection seems to be that sin comes first and the devil enters afterwards.
Moses' "Holy and righteous is the Lord" is Deuteronomy 32:4 in the Septuagint's wording.
The section begins and ends mid-sentence where the source does.

title: True generation from God through faith and works
english: Having received the Holy Spirit from the Lord, many false apostles were driven by the devil, pretending to teach the gospel. It is necessary to have that gift of the Holy Spirit, which is named the discernment of spirits, so that we may have knowledge to test the spirits (1 John 4:1), so as for one to believe and for the other to resist.

For there came some who were saying in a human fantasy that the Lord had descended from heaven, whose glories the Manichaeans confirmed. Having understood this: 'It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me' (Gal 2:20), through accepting Christ Jesus living in me, through carrying around the death of Jesus in the body (2 Corinthians 4:10); confessing that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh (1 John 4:2), not by his own alone, but also in mine.

He calls characteristic of the antichrist, of whom we have heard that he is coming, but is already in the world (1 John 4:3), the denying the incarnation of Jesus through false prophets and spirits in not confessing that he has come in the flesh; to say this is now truly to be heard; for many say it by tongue alone.

Just as a crime and arrogance brings to the one not taking up the excellent and not loving the lovable, so the writer makes praise for those loving the worthy of being loved to be beloved; but when can this happen, except when the Savior takes away the sin of the world (John 1:29), so that the man may be shown as what he has become by God according to likeness and having been shown an image of the Maker? For when the man is revealed, being immediately beloved and worthy of being loved, he becomes so; since therefore the Savior sent to the world, through love toward the works of the Father which are his own, came for the showing of the beauty of those who have become according to the image of God, those possessing this gift are beloved, whence they love one another; for each has both being the beloved and being the loving, having the commandment to love the neighbor.

If love is from God and God is love (1 John 4:7–8), who would be the one proceeding from him or the Word himself? If anyone therefore has love, he has Christ in himself; namely, he who said: 'God is love' (1 John 4:8), he again knew.
A love from God, which must be considered as nothing other than the Only-begotten, just as God is from God, so also is a love existing from love.
Those being born from God through uprightness according to virtue are these, and they are children of God and friends, just as Abraham was (Gen 15:6).

He who is born from God, having believed that Jesus is the Christ (1 John 5:1), is not born from God having a mere mental assent regarding the preaching of the Christ, but rather that faith which is joined to works according to virtue; which Abraham, having, was reckoned to have righteousness (Gen 15:6). According to this, the thing signified is to be accepted: 'to find a faithful man'; for such a one is rarely found, among many being eager but having a dead faith without works, which is not even at all faith. He who has believed thus, as to be born from God, has eternal life, as the Savior says: 'he who believes in me has eternal life' (John 3:36); if indeed someone is born from God by acting uprightly in the things said, being worthy of acceptance, he must love also him who begot him before that.

And the substance, and—so that I may phrase it this way—the matter which must have love toward God, he says is the keeping of the divine commandments (1 John 5:3); which things carry up to God the [virtues] acting through them; whence they are neither useless nor heavy.

If indeed anyone, coming to them, says they are heavy in a way other than what is required, he blamed his own weakness; for it is considered a friend to those who excessively cast off strength to think [commandments] heavy and everything light and trivial; whence he did not write: 'his commandments are light', but: 'they are not heavy' alone, and of one perceiving everything, having known through experience the just pursuing the just despite their uselessness, that the yoke of Christ is light, having much kindness (Matt 11:30). He who is thus disposed is born from God, and having obtained this, he despises the life of the entering [world] and the pleasant things of the world; and by this he conquers the world, having passed from it into a super-cosmic citizenship. This thus progressing in faith will work even toward righteousness reckoned as such; which he also shows as having been established and remaining, saying: 'this is the victory that has conquered the world' (1 John 5:4); which faith we have, having adhered to Jesus being the Son of God.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The World's Hatred and the Mind of Christ
english: Those who have learned by practice how each of the diligent in good things succeeds become hopeful of enduring these things again and at other times; for even the holy apostles and the blessed John, by whose works they knew that they had often asked God as a friend and desired one, are courageous that, asking in this way every time, they will obtain what they desire from the leaning God (1 John 5:14–15).

From these things it will be shown how the things sought by some are true; 'the one asking receives' (Luke 11:10) does not mean that all people, asking haphazardly, receive the same things that do not benefit them, but rather those containing [the request] according to the will of God. Such boldness approaches one living a life beyond understanding; but such a person is rare; 'for who shall boast of having a pure heart?' (Proverbs 20:9); for few are those existing thus in virtue, as it is said: 'if I had seen injustice in my heart, Lord, do not listen to me; because of this, he listened to me' (Psalm 66:18-19), since he did not see injustice; but he desisted from fear that he might be judged according to the one saying: 'I do not know myself; but not in this am I justified' (1 Corinthians 4:4); he takes up what is set forth and also: 'if our heart does not condemn us, we have boldness toward God' (1 John 3:21).

For if being from God comes from doing righteousness, as we have often said, but it is impossible to sin and practice righteousness at the same time, it is therefore evident that one thus disposed and acting is just and does not sin; then, securing the position that man is a choosing being and not a son of God by nature, he appropriately added: 'but he guards himself, and the evil one does not touch him' (1 John 5:18); for if because of this the evil one does not touch him, that he guards himself, he has the not-sinning not from construction, but from attentiveness; and if someone is guarding himself, what does he pray to God for? That he might remain entirely unswayed by the evil one.

Having learned through many those bad men who are made manifest by the voice of the world, we do not stand in awe like the heretics, lest the creation of God, being a world, be established in the evil one (1 John 5:19); the voice of the world lies upon men, as has been said, and here also in the gospels; it writes...

For John says, “Do not marvel if the world hates you” (1 John 3:13); it is clear to everyone possessing understanding that the world hates the holy, meaning the wicked men. And he adds, “They are of the world and the world hears them” (1 John 4:5); for the world that hears those speaking deceitfully signifies not the creation, but the people moved by passions.

He gave a mind, by which the true one, having come as the Son of God, is known (1 John 5:20); this is the same as to say, “But we have the mind of Christ.” He who possesses this very mind and this very intellect knows the one who is true according to essence and is united to him, truly having his understanding.

How then, having testified to this perfection through the whole epistle, does he now exhort them to keep themselves from idols (1 John 5:21)? We say therefore: since it was written to the whole church, and it was likely in such a gathering to be now standing apart from idolatry, for their sake he engraved the word.

What is set forth agrees with what was said in the first epistle, having it thus: “And we know that he who loves [God] keeps the commandments”; and the Lord: “If anyone loves me, he will keep my commandments.” Walking according to the commandments is the same as keeping them (2 John 1:6); for the virtues practiced according to the commandments are a walking, for he who does not remain outside of them walks according to them; and in this, keeping them is the same. Therefore, he who has ceased to act according to virtue no longer keeps the commandments nor walks according to them. For he who progresses according to virtue walks according to the commandments, showing progress, and he who has been perfected after having walked according to the commandments keeps them. With this, what was said enigmatically agrees, how Adam was placed in Paradise to work and to keep, him showing progress through his working, and the keeping signifying permanence in perfection.

He remains in the evangelical teaching, he who thinks and acts according to it (2 John 1:9), but he who acts and glorifies contrary to it departs from it. Then, since through the practical and the theoretical, God the Creator of all things becomes [known] as [it was] with Abraham...
